thread:
maria: Quick UX proposal — add a timeline panel in Console for automatic fallback policy events. Show SLO lines (p99 latency), error-rate, and markers for when fallback/degrade modes kicked in. Click an event to open the audit record + sample request.

alex: +1. Do we want to show trigger reason on hover? e.g. '5xx rate > 3%', 'latency spike', 'quota exceeded'.

jordan: Hover reason is good. Also suggest an adjustable sampling window so operators can inspect pre/post windows (30s/5m/15m).

maria: Yes — timeline should default to 5m pre / 2m post around the event. And let users expand to custom ranges. Important for debugging cascading fallbacks.

sam: Can we wire the timeline to the rollout history view? I want to see fallback events mapped to specific rollout versions and routes.

maria: Exactly. Map each fallback marker to (model-version, route, policy-id). Clicking opens the rollout detail panel.

alex: UX nit — use stacked mini-charts per route (small multiples) rather than a single dense chart. Easier to scan which route caused the fallback.

jordan: For auditability, we need a direct link to the underlying policy decision record (signed event with operator overrides). Ops must be able to see who approved any sticky override.

opsbot: policy-evaluator: Fallback triggered policy=autofallback-03 reason=\"latency_p99>1200ms\" route=\"/chat/gen\" rollout=rv-2026-03-22-2 sample_id=cntrl-4590

maria: Can the UI surface the sample request inline (sanitized) and the model outputs that were returned? That would speed triage.

sam: Need guardrails — redact PII automatically and only show up to first 3 tokens of user content unless operator has explicit permission.

alex: Telemetry question — what ingest do we need? We should capture (timestamp, route, policy_id, trigger_reason, p99, qps, ops_override, trace_id). Queryable in Console and exportable to CSV.

jordan: Also capture correlated infra signals (gpu util, node OOMs). Sometimes fallback is infra-triggered.

maria: Agree. We'll add a small infra ribbon on the timeline.

sam: How do we handle quotas? If fallback was due to quota exhaustion on Dedicated, we should show capacity vs committed reserved.

maria: Add a capacity overlay when policy scope includes dedicated pools. Show commit line and current utilization.

alex: Implementation idea — backend emits a structured event to audit-log with a compact JSON. UI loads events and runs client-side small queries to build the timeline. Example event:

```
{
  \"ts\": 1708452345,
  \"route\": \"/chat/gen\",
  \"policy_id\": \"autofallback-03\",
  \"reason\": \"latency_p99>1200ms\",
  \"p99\": 1390,
  \"qps\": 120,
  \"model_version\": \"rv-2026-03-22-2\",
  \"trace_id\": \"tr-8a7f\",
  \"operator\": \"-\",
  \"override\": false
}
```

alex: That should be light enough for high-throughput ingestion.

jordan: One more ops flow: allow creating a short-lived 'investigation' snapshot when operator clicks an event. Snapshot stores samples and telemetry for 24h for postmortem exports.

maria: For the rollout UI, we should add a 'replay' button that replays timeline events in fast-forward to show cascading fallbacks across routes. Helpful in postmortem.

sam: UX + security: only users with the 'oncall' or 'se' role can trigger a replay or download snapshots. Others see a redacted preview.

opsbot: note: export-snapshot created snapshot_id=snap-20260322-01 by user=sam expires_in=86400

maria: Cool. I'll mock screens for the timeline, stacked charts, infra ribbon, and the event detail drawer. Will post a prototype later today.

alex: Thanks — once we have the mock, we can sync with infra for the event schema and with telemetry for sampling windows.

jordan: +1 to sync. Also will add an acceptance criterion: timeline loads under 1s for 30 events.

maria: Great — tagging follow-ups: @alex to event schema, @jordan telemetry contract, @sam permissions/exports.

sam: on it. :thumbsup:

maria: (GIF: tiny parachute)
